name: Shrewsbury
headline: A closer look at Shrewsbury,
from the lakeshore to Main Street.
answer: Shrewsbury is a Worcester County town of 38,325 people (2020 Census), across Lake Quinsigamond from Worcester. Single-family homes grew along its 19th-century streetcar routes, and The Warren Group counted 234 single-family sales in 2025. I-290, Route 9, Route 20 and Route 140 cross the town; the nearest commuter rail stops are in neighboring Worcester, Grafton and Westborough.
overview: Shrewsbury sits just east of Worcester, with Lake Quinsigamond between them; I-290 crosses the water into town. Shrewsbury was incorporated in 1727 and grew along the old Boston Post Road, where two milestones from 1767 still stand. In the 19th century, streetcar lines helped single-family housing spread outward from the center, while the lakeshore filled with cottages and a summer resort season. The White City amusement park once stood by the lake; a shopping plaza holds the site today.

Main Street is the town's historic spine. The General Artemas Ward House Museum, a Harvard-affiliated house museum at 786 Main Street, opens for free guided tours from mid-April through November, across the road from Dean Park and its trails. Prospect Park adds 71 acres of forest paths, Jordan Pond has about 0.8 miles of trails, and Ski Ward at 1000 Main Street runs skiing, snowboarding and tubing through the year. The public library moved into a new 42,000-square-foot building in 2016.

Lake Quinsigamond, about 4 miles long and 772 acres, lies between Shrewsbury and Worcester, and getting across it shaped the town. After a bridge collapsed in 1817, a floating bridge served until 1861, an earthen causeway was finished in 1863, and a stone, cement and steel bridge opened in 1919; most lakeside building clustered on the southern shores once the causeway was in place. Competitive rowing on the lake dates to 1857, and it hosts college regattas including the Eastern Sprints. On the Shrewsbury side, the town lists the Donahue Rowing Center and the Corazzini Boat Ramp on North Quinsigamond Avenue and a second ramp at Oak Island on Route 20.

housing.text: Streetcar routes in the 19th century propelled the growth of single-family housing in Shrewsbury, and lakeside cottages were built along Lake Quinsigamond. The Warren Group recorded 234 single-family sales in town in 2025.

villages.name: Shrewsbury Historic District
villages.line: About 14 acres around the common laid out in 1721 at Main and Prospect Streets, with the 1766 First Congregational Church, an 1830 brick schoolhouse now used for town offices and the historical society, the 1797 Sumner House and the 1903 library building; listed on the National Register in 1976.

commute.text: Shrewsbury has no commuter rail station of its own; the Framingham/Worcester Line stops in neighboring Worcester, Grafton and Westborough. I-290 has two Shrewsbury exits, at Main Street and Route 140, and Route 9, Route 20 and Route 140 also cross the town.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Shrewsbury, MA?
faq.a: The median single-family sale price in Shrewsbury for calendar year 2025 was $716,500, across 234 sales, compared with $675,000 in 2024, according to The Warren Group's MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town report.
Not within town. The MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line stops in neighboring Worcester, Grafton (at 1 Pine Street in North Grafton) and Westborough.
Shrewsbury Public Schools. Review its profile with DESE.

faq.q: How do you cross Lake Quinsigamond between Shrewsbury and Worcester?
faq.a: Route 9 crosses on the Kenneth F. Burns Memorial Bridge, a steel arch bridge with a separate structure for each direction that opened in November 2015, and I-290 crosses on its own bridge at the north end of the lake.

faq.q: What is the property tax rate in Shrewsbury, MA?
faq.a: According to the Massachusetts Division of Local Services, Shrewsbury's FY2026 residential property tax rate is $11.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, the same rate for all property classes. No residential exemption is noted in the sources used for this guide; the Assessors' Office handles personal exemptions, such as those for seniors and veterans.
